title: Fire Emblem's Black Sheep Stayed in Japan for 25 Years
hook:
In 1992 Nintendo shipped a Fire Emblem so odd it stayed locked in Japan for 25 years, until Echoes rebuilt it in 2017 and opened at number one there with over 130,000 copies in a week. Which Fire Emblem deserves the next remake?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Fire Emblem's strangest game stayed locked in Japan for twenty five years? Fire Emblem Gaiden hit the Famicom in Japan on March 14, 1992. It was only the second game in the series, and it threw out most of the first game's rules. You walked across a world map, explored towns, and crawled through dungeons. Two heroes, Alm and Celica, each led their own army down separate paths. Mages learned spells by leveling up instead of carrying tomes. Fans called it the black sheep of the series. It never left Japan, and it still is not on Nintendo Switch Online. Then in twenty seventeen, Nintendo and Intelligent Systems rebuilt it for the 3DS as Fire Emblem Echoes, Shadows of Valentia. It launched in Japan on April twentieth and in the West on May nineteenth. It was the first Fire Emblem with full voice acting, with nearly every line spoken out loud. It also added Mila's Turnwheel, a rewind button for undoing your mistakes. In Japan it debuted at number one and sold over one hundred thirty thousand copies in its first week. It was the last mainline Fire Emblem on the 3DS. Which Fire Emblem deserves a remake next? Follow for more gaming history.
